record.paper_title: Known Results and Open Problems on C1 linearization in Banach Spaces
record.original_question: For the problem of C^1 linearization of contractions on infinite-dimensional Banach spaces, can one construct sharper counterexamples than the existing ones? In particular, is there a counterexample of the type described after Theorem 6 with r=0, or even a counterexample whose linear part A has spectral modulus set |σ(A)| = [ab,b] ∪ {a} for some real numbers 0 < b < a < 1?

evidence.quote: Problem 1: Better counter-examples. A better understanding of the non-resonance conditions (2) needs better counterexamples. It would be good to have a counterexample as in Theorem 6 but with r = 0. Or, even better, a counterexample with |σ(A)| = [ab, b]∪ {a}, with 0 < b < a < 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space and let $F: U \to X$ be a $C^{1,1}$ map defined on a neighborhood $U$ of $0$ with $F(0)=0$, such that $A := DF(0)$ is a bounded linear contraction (i.e. its spectral radius is $<1$). One says $F$ is $C^1$-linearizable at $0$ if there exists a local $C^1$ diffeomorphism $H$ fixing $0$ such that $H\circ F = A\circ H$ near $0$.

Known counterexamples to $C^1$ linearization rely on certain non-resonance-type conditions on the spectrum $\sigma(A)$. A typical such counterexample requires $\sigma(A)$ to have a specific shape: writing $|\sigma(A)| = \{|\lambda| : \lambda \in \sigma(A)\} \subset (0,1)$, the construction uses spectra of the form $|\sigma(A)| = [a b^{1+r}, b] \cup \{a\}$ with $0 < b < a < 1$ and some parameter $r > 0$ measuring how far one is from the borderline case.

Question. Within this framework, can one construct sharper counterexamples to $C^1$ linearization? Specifically:

(a) Is there a $C^{1,1}$ map $F$ on an infinite-dimensional Banach space with $F(0)=0$, whose linear part $A = DF(0)$ has $|\sigma(A)| = [a b^{1+r}, b] \cup \{a\}$ with $r = 0$ (i.e. $|\sigma(A)| = [ab, b] \cup \{a\}$ but realized in the limiting case where the standard construction breaks down), and such that $F$ is not $C^1$-linearizable at $0$?

(b) More strongly, is there such an $F$ whose linear part $A$ satisfies exactly $|\sigma(A)| = [ab, b] \cup \{a\}$ for some $0 < b < a < 1$, and which is not $C^1$-linearizable at $0$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published construction of the requested sharper counterexamples (either the $r=0$ case or a counterexample with $|\sigma(A)| = [ab,b]\cup\{a\}$). Related literature on $C^{k,1}$ contractions and spectral-gap/band conditions on Banach spaces appears, but no resolution of this specific question was found, so the status is taken as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Local Contractions of Banach Spaces and Spectral Gap Conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses C^1 linearization of contractions in Banach spaces under spectral gap / non-resonance conditions.
status_evidence.claim: The framework of spectral gap and non-resonance conditions for C^1 linearization on Banach spaces is established, but no counterexample of the requested sharper form is reported.

status_evidence.title: Sharp regularity of linearization for C^{1,1} hyperbolic diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Studies regularity of linearization for C^{1,1} hyperbolic diffeomorphisms, with spectral band conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Related sharpness results exist, but a counterexample with |σ(A)| = [ab,b] ∪ {a} or with r=0 is not provided.
